messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Livepager: p99 tail latency breach detected in us-west2 ingress (router) — alerting oncall maria. p95 820ms -> 910ms, p99 4.2s -> 5.9s, streaming stall rate +14% in last 5m. Auto-bridge created.

maria: seeing it. I’m on the bridge. tagging eng-runtime and oncall-sre. Initial dashboard: spike started ~4750004230 (2m before pager). Heap of requests hitting a small set of router instances.

raj: joining. Can someone post the top routing policy diff from the last deploy? I suspect the new weight-balancer change we rolled out earlier.

sophie: looking now. Push from deploy ci at 4750004000 included change: routing.policy.prefer_local set to false for the canary region, and a new seed entropy tweak. Pasting diff:
```
- prefer_local: true
+ prefer_local: false
# added weight-sink fallback: region_weight_bias=0.12
```

tom: ok that aligns. Telemetry shows a ~73% increase in session affinity to two router IDs in us-west2 (router-uw2-03, router-uw2-08). Those nodes show high CPU and long tail queuing.

maria: customers? beth_cs — any reports upstream from support?

beth_cs: few customers flagged streaming stalls (video transcript streaming and long-poll features). A high-volume SaaS customer in EU reported timeouts for clients routed via us-west2 (they saw retries). No major revenue impact yet but degraded UX.

raj: hypothesis: policy change reduced cross-zone preference, causing a hotbucketing effect (traffic collapsed to fewer router cores). That + continuous batching for streaming endpoints is causing KV cache thrash -> tail.

sophie: checking KV hit rates. Cache miss rate on router-uw2-03 spiked from 6% -> 42% over the window, and backend pods show increased cold-starts for stream sessions.

maria: mitigation idea A: re-enable prefer_local=true to rebalance cross-zone routing; mitigation B: apply emergency weight-split rule to smooth weight across routers; mitigation C: route streaming->fallback model instance pool as temporary.

raj: can we do A quickly? Is the flag a config-on-the-fly? Sophie?

sophie: prefer_local is a runtime flag that can be toggled via config service. I can flip it back globally for us-west2 in ~30s with no deploy. Doing it now: `curl -X POST https://config.internal/flags/routing/prefer_local -d '{"region":"us-west2","value":true}'`

ops-bot: config change accepted. prefer_local=true for region us-west2 will propagate in 20s.

maria: everyone watch metrics. Also set emergency retry window to avoid thundering retries: reduce client retry burst for streaming to 50ms jitter.

tom: implementing per-route retry header on the edge LB for streaming. Pushing change now.

sophie: prefer_local propagated. Initial signs: the traffic fan-out increased to more router instances, CPU distribution smoothing. Recomputing p99 in 1m.

maria: p95 now 760ms, p99 down to 2.1s (from 5.9s). Streaming stall delta down to +4%. Good progress.

raj: while we stabilize, let's also pin the routing policy on the canary rollout to previous version until we can fully vet the seed/weight bias. Who owns the rollout? Sophie?

sophie: I’ll open a rollback PR and hold canary. Also capturing the deploy id: ci/2026-03-15-1745.

beth_cs: notifying impacted customers that we've mitigated a routing skew and are continuing to monitor. Will update support thread.

maria: assigning action items: raj -> deep router logs + queue diagnostics for router-uw2-03/08; sophie -> rollback canary and add more telemetry around seed entropy; tom -> confirm retry header change across all edge LB nodes; beth_cs -> customer comms. We’ll reconvene in 20m for status and decide on postmortem.

raj: grabbing logs now. Noting a recurring pattern: requests with large streaming prefills (>8k tokens) get queued longer due to chunked batching thresholds hitting a single router; batching window and affinity caused batching group to concentrate.

sophie: adding a temporary guard in the kernel selection to bypass aggressive batching for streaming endpoints in us-west2 (hotfix). Deploying a canary hotfix to 10% of routers now.

ops-bot: hotfix rollout to routers-10% started. ETA 40s.

maria: live update: p99 stable ~1.9s, p95 700ms, streaming stalls back to baseline +1%. Looks like prefer_local revert + retry cap fixed the tail.

beth_cs: support updated customers w/ status: "We saw localized routing skew affecting some streaming requests; we've mitigated and are monitoring. No data loss."

raj: will leave traces and dump of queue histograms to /var/logs/incident/4750004321 for post-incident analysis. Also saving router snapshots and routing table versions.

maria: thank you all. Formal incident postmortem owners: raj (root cause analysis), sophie (rollback & rollout process), tom (edge retry policy), beth_cs (customer impact summary). I'll file the incident ticket and set a follow-up review in 48h. If anyone sees regression ping this thread.

incident-bot: Incident closed to livepager but thread remains for follow-up. Timeline: escalated 4750004321 -> mitigated 4750004440. Please attach any artifacts to ticket #INC-2026-03-15-07.

maria: closing notes: short-term mitigation successful; RCA points: routing policy change + seed/weight bias caused traffic concentration -> cache thrash -> tail. Long-term tasks: add rollout gating for seed/weight changes, more simulation for streaming workloads, and auto-smoothing fallback when hotbucket detection triggers.
